chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the one who murdered, drank wine, and stole, so he established the Penalty (Hadd) upon him. So he whipped him due to his drinking the wine, and cut his hand regarding his theft, and killed him due to his committing murder.

key_terms.الْحَدَّ: The fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia

ai.seo_question: How are multiple Hadd penalties applied to a single person who commits murder, theft, and drinking wine?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'accumulation of penalties' (ta'addud al-hudud) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam Ali (peace be upon him) applied distinct punishments for murder, drinking, and theft without one absorbing the other. It serves as a foundational precedent for understanding how multiple hudud can be executed sequentially on a single individual, reflecting the comprehensive nature of divine justice in the early Islamic community.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zurara Bin Muhammad, from Sama’at,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws judged regarding the one who murdered, and drank wine, and stole, so heasws established the Penalty (Hadd) upon him. So heasws whipped him due to his drinking the wine, and cut his hand regarding his theft, and killed him due to his comitting murder’.
